name: Facial yoga / face exercises

card.summary: Muscle exercises for the face promoted as a natural facelift; the available sources include no study of appearance outcomes.
card.aka: face yoga, facial exercises, face workouts
card.note: Sources reviewed contain no study measuring appearance change; forum members themselves rank exercises below surgery or appliances.

quick.overview:
Facial yoga and face exercises are routines of deliberate facial-muscle movements, often shown on video, that proponents say tone the cheeks, chin and jaw and soften the signs of ageing. Looksmaxxing communities discuss them as a low-cost option for the cheekbones, chin and jawline.

No clinical study of their effect on appearance is available among the sources used here. Research that exists on facial exercises concerns older adults' mental health, not facial appearance.
quick.mechanism: The idea is that strengthening facial muscles lifts and fills the overlying skin, much as exercise builds other muscles. Forum users who discuss the topic add that fat loss and chewing are what change facial shape, and some describe the exercises as a fallback for people who cannot afford surgery.
quick.risks: No documented harms appear in the sources used. A forum guide describes the exercises as inferior to surgery, appliances or fillers and as better than nothing for young or low-budget users.

lead: Facial yoga, also called face exercises, is a set of voluntary facial-muscle movements promoted to firm, lift or reshape the face, and is often presented as a natural alternative to cosmetic procedures. In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed for the cheekbones, nose, chin and jawline [1][2].

None of the studies identified for this article tested facial exercises for facial appearance. Small studies of facial exercise programmes in older adults examined mental health and cognition rather than looks [3][4].

paras: Routines combine exaggerated expressions, tongue and jaw movements and resistance techniques, usually taught by video. One forum guide breaks them into targets for the cheekbones, nose, chin and jawline, including a weighted variation of mewing [1].

No studies found on facial exercises for appearance. A Japanese study of 75 community-dwelling adults aged 65 to 87 assessed the effect of facial exercises on mental health [3], and a trial in elderly people with mild cognitive impairment compared walking with hand and face exercises for executive function [4]. A Time magazine article on facial yoga appeared in 2007 [5]. These did not measure facial appearance.

One widely read forum guide describes face exercises as 'copefuel', ranking surgery above appliances, fillers and exercises for results, but says that for young or low-budget people the exercises are better than nothing, and that a chin routine produced results for the author [1]. A reply in the same thread said the only things that work are losing fat or gaining jaw muscle from chewing [1]. Another thread asks whether a set of exercises is 'legit' and draws jokes rather than evidence [2].

lore.intro: Face exercises sit at the bottom of the community's usual ranking of methods, behind surgery, appliances and fillers, and are mostly recommended to people with limited options [1].

claims.claim: Chin and jaw exercises can produce visible change
claims.believers: A guide's author says a chin exercise produced results quickly for him, advising it for mildly recessed chins [1].
claims.experts: No published study has measured appearance change from facial exercises; existing studies concern older adults' mental health and cognition [3][4].

claims.claim: Face exercises are a lesser substitute for surgery or appliances
claims.believers: The same guide says results from surgery, appliances and fillers always exceed exercises [1].

claims.claim: Fat loss and chewing do more than face exercises
claims.believers: A reply says the only effective approaches are losing fat or building jaw muscle by chewing [1].
claims.experts: Masseter enlargement from heavy chewing is documented, but not as an exercise programme tested for appearance.
